Fourier Series expansion contains no terms of frequency $\omega = 2\pi$(2k)/T;  k=1,2...  Also, no sine terms are present. Then x(t) satisfies the equation

detailed_solution.markdown:
Since trigonometric fourier series has no sine terms and has only cosine terms therefore this will be an even signal i.e. it will satisfy.

$x(t)=x(-t)$

or, we can write,

$x(t-T)=x(-t+T)$

but signal is periodic with period T.

therefore $x(t-T)=x(t)$

therefore,  $x(t)=x(T-t)\;\;...(i)$

Now, since signal contains only odd harmonics i.e. no terms of frequency

As capacitor is charged initially to voltage $V_0$, then representation of capacitor in s-domain As current through the inductor is zero at t=0, then The circuit at $t \gt 0$ $I(s)=\frac{V_0/s}{\frac{1}{sC}+sL}=\frac{V_0}{s^2L+\frac{1}{C}} I(s)=\frac{V_0}{L}\left ( \frac{1}{s^2+\frac{1}{LC}} \right ) Voltage across capacitor =voltage across inductor [latex]=V(s),$ $V(s)=I(s) \times (sL)$ $\;\;=\frac{V_0}{L}\left ( \frac{1}{s^2+\frac{1}{LC}} \right ) \times (sL)$ $\;\;=V_0\left ( \frac{s}{s^2+\frac{1}{LC}} \right )$ As, $\omega _0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$ $V(s)=V_0\left ( \frac{s}{s^2+\omega _0^2} \right )$ Voltage across the capacitor $=V(t)=L^{-1}[V(s)]$ $\;\;=L^{-1}\left ( \frac{V_0s}{s^2+\omega _0^2} \right )$ $V(t)=V_0 \cos \omega _0 t$ where, $\omega _0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} N_{s_1} &=\frac{120f_1}{P} \\ &= \frac{120 \times 50}{4}=1500\; \text{rpm}\\ s_1 &=\frac{N_{s_1}-N_{R_1}}{N_{s_1}} \\ &= \frac{1500-1440}{1500}=0.04\\ \text{as}\;\;\frac{V}{f} &=\text{Constant} \\ \frac{V_1}{f_1}&=\frac{V_2}{f_2} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; V_2&=V_1\left ( \frac{f_2}{f_1} \right ) \\ &= 400 \times \frac{30}{50}=240V \end{aligned}$$ Torque developed in induction motor $T=\frac{3}{\omega _s}\frac{V^2R'_2/s}{(R'_2/s)^2 +{X'_2}^2}$ In stable region, slip is very low, so $\frac{R'_2}{s} \gt \gt X'_2$ So, T can be approximated as $$\begin{aligned} T &=\frac{3}{\omega _s}\frac{V^2R'_2/s}{(R'_2/s)^2} \\ &=\frac{3}{\omega _s} \frac{8V^2}{R'_2} \\ T&\propto \frac{sV^2}{f} \\ \frac{T_1}{T_2}&= \frac{s_1}{s_2}\left ( \frac{V_1}{V_2} \right )^2 \times \frac{f_2}{f_1} \end{aligned}$$ as load torque is constant, $T_1=T_2$ $$\begin{aligned} s_2 &=s_1 \left ( \frac{V_1}{V_2} \right )^2 \times \frac{f_2}{f_1}\\ &= 0.04 \times \left ( \frac{400}{240} \right )^2 \times \left ( \frac{30}{50} \right )\\ &= 0.067\\ N_{s2} &=\frac{120f_2}{P} \\ &= \frac{120 \times 30}{4}=900 \; \text{rpm}\\ &\text {Rotor speed,}\\ N_{r2}&=N_{s2(1-s_2)} \\ &= 900(1-0.067)\\ &\approx 840 \; \text{rpm} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

RMS value of source current

RMS value of $n^{th}$ harmonic

pitch factor due to fundamental component

A voltage commutated chopper operating at 1 kHz is used to control the speed of dc as shown in figure. The load current is assumed to be constant at 10 A.

The minimum time in $\mu$ sec for which the SCR M should be ON is

detailed_solution.markdown: Initially, main thyristor (m) and auxiliary thyristor (A) are off and capacitor is assumed charged to voltage V with upper plate positive. When 'm' is turned on at t=0, source voltage V is applied across load and load current $I_0$ begins to flow which is assumed to remain constant. With 'm' ON at t=0, anotheroscillatory circuit consisting of C, m, L and D is formed where the capacitor current is given by $i_c=V\sqrt{\frac{C}{L}} \sin \omega _0 t=I_p \sin \omega _0 t$ When, $\omega _0 t=\pi, i_c=0$ Between $0 \\lt t \\lt \frac{\pi}{\omega _0}, i_{T1}=I_0+I_P \sin \omega _0 t$ capacitor voltage charges from $+V_s \; to \; -V_s$ sinusoidally and the lower plate becomes positive. At $\omega _0 t=\pi, i_c=0, i_{T1}=I_0 \text{ and }V_c=-V_s$ At $t_1$, thyristor A is turned on and capacitor voltage V applies a reverse voltage across thyristor in and SCR 'm' is turned off. The load current is now carried by C and SCR A. So, minimum time for which SCR 'm' should be ON. $$\begin{aligned} T_{min}&=\frac{\pi}{\omega _0}=\pi\sqrt{LC} \\ &= \pi\sqrt{2 \times 10^{-3} \times 1 \times 10^{-6}}=140\mu s \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
